description: A connection pool configuration spec defines a valid PgBouncer (or equivalent) pool policy — mode, sizing, auth, health checking, and idle management — such that the pool never exhausts PostgreSQL max_connections.

rules.description: The spec must declare pool_mode, max_client_connections, default_pool_size, reserve_pool_size, server_idle_timeout, auth_type, health_check_query, max_db_connections, and pools array.
pool_mode must be session, transaction, or statement. Any other value is rejected by PgBouncer and causes silent fallback to session mode.

The sum of all pool sizes plus reserve_pool_size must not exceed (max_db_connections - reserved_system_connections). Exceeding this hard limit causes PostgreSQL to reject connections with FATAL: too many connections.
max_client_connections must be greater than the sum of all pool sizes. This ensures clients can queue when all pool slots are busy rather than being immediately rejected.
auth_type must be scram-sha-256. MD5 is deprecated, vulnerable to offline cracking from challenge-response captures, and disabled by default in PostgreSQL 16+.
health_check_query must be a non-empty SQL string. Without it, stale server connections silently accumulate in the pool and cause unexpected connection close errors.
reserve_pool_size must be > 0. A zero reserve means clients are hard-rejected when all pool slots are occupied — no graceful degradation is possible.
server_idle_timeout must be a positive number >= 30 seconds. Zero disables timeout and causes connection exhaustion; values below 30s cause excessive churn.
